incidente.resumo: A GitHub personal access token with recently elevated scopes was leaked from Homebrew's Jenkins, giving git push access to Homebrew/brew and Homebrew/homebrew-core; a security researcher found and reported it. Within a few hours the credentials were revoked, replaced and sanitised within Jenkins, and GitHub Support verified the token had not been used to push to those repositories during the period of elevated scopes.

descricao.texto: On 31 July 2018 a security researcher identified the leaked GitHub personal access token and reported it to Homebrew's HackerOne.
trechos: On 31st July 2018 a security researcher identified a GitHub personal access token with recently elevated scopes was leaked from Homebrew’s Jenkins that gave them access to git push on Homebrew/brew and Homebrew/homebrew-core.
They reported this to our Hacker One.

acoes.texto: Already done: Homebrew/brew and Homebrew/homebrew-core were updated so non-administrators cannot push directly to master.
trechos: Homebrew/brew and Homebrew/homebrew-core were updated so non-administrators on those repositories cannot push directly to master.

acoes.texto: Already done: most repositories in the Homebrew organisation (not Homebrew/homebrew-core) were updated to require CI checks from a pull request to pass before changes can be pushed to master; branch protection and required reviews were enabled on additional repositories.
trechos: Most repositories in the Homebrew organisation (notably not Homebrew/homebrew-core due to their current workflow and maintainer requests) were also updated to require CI checks from a pull request to pass before changes can be pushed to master.
We enabled branch protection and required reviews on additional repositories as mentioned above.

acoes.texto: Already done: all Homebrew maintainers were requested to review and prune their personal access tokens and disable SMS fallback for 2FA.
trechos: We requested all Homebrew maintainers review and prune their personal access tokens and disable SMS fallback for 2FA.

acoes.texto: Already in place for several years: 2FA and third party application restrictions for the entire Homebrew GitHub organisation, which the security researcher also recommended.
trechos: We have for several years enabled 2FA and third party application restrictions for the entire Homebrew GitHub organisation. This was also recommended by the security researcher.

observacoes: No malicious use is reported: GitHub Support verified the token was not used to push to Homebrew/brew or Homebrew/homebrew-core during the period of elevated scopes, and the text says no packages were compromised. The security researcher also recommended GPG signing for Homebrew/homebrew-core; the project leadership committee rejected it in a non-unanimous vote due to workflow concerns. The text ends with a call for contributions, on-call volunteers and Patreon donations.
